cells.tense: The light is still there and the walking toward it is still yours to give.
cells.ask: At the end of the day, say out loud what still pulls you. Name it once to one person, or write it where only you will see.
cells.core:
You are still going toward the thing. Not running at it the way you would have at the start, and not wandering either — years in, you have found a pace that holds. The pull has not thinned. What you steer by is more rock than ever, because it has survived long enough to look plain.

Other people get to see what this makes. The part nobody watches is what it asks of you: keeping a light alive through a season when it does not show on the surface. You can feed one thing this way without pushing it. Pick the next stretch ahead. Let the pace you have already proved be enough to carry it.
cells.sheetLine: You are still going. The pace now is the proof.
cells.verb: holding to the light that was chosen when it cannot be seen
cells.place: standing in front of what pulls you forward, where the pull is still there and the going is not

cells.tense: You are already holding how the next part will go before any of it has arrived.
cells.ask: Pick the next thing that comes up because you want it to, and do only that, with the part after it left for later.
cells.core:
You are with something that has not happened yet, steadying yourself against it before it arrives. The persistence that brought you here is still running, and it has started working ahead — bracing for the next pressure, the next stretch that asks for proof. You carry more of a future that is not written than anyone can see.

What that does is spend the patience you built on a scene that has not come. The going itself is being paid for in advance. Notice once today when you are holding something that isn't here yet. Let one step go unwatched. The light still comes up whether you rehearsed it or not.
cells.sheetLine: You are bracing for a season that has not arrived.

cells.tense: The light is still there, and the walking toward it stopped with you still standing.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did, however small, in the last week that kept you standing. Say it to one person or write it down today.
cells.core:
You know what pulls you. That has not gone anywhere. What has gone quiet is the walking — the days when the pull came out in a step. Going after it takes holding the light up where it can't be seen, and something in you has stopped lifting it. The door you came out of is behind you and the room stays warm.

The pull is still there. What went missing is the hands. You do not have to feel anything or want anything more than you do right now. One thing you did this week kept you standing, even carried badly. Write it on paper where you can see it. Not the want first — the weight.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see the light. Your hands stopped doing it.
cells.verb: holding to the light that was chosen when it cannot be seen

cells.tense: You are already keeping the light going, and you have been calling it the concern of other people.
cells.ask: Take one thing you are carrying and use one hour on it today as if you had chosen it, not because it fell on you.
cells.core:
You are the one carrying this, and it has been that way for a long time. In how you show up, in what you take on, in what you keep going when nobody asks — the persistence is running. What is missing is the stamp. You describe it as assigned, or as just being practical, and someone else gets the credit for what you have held.

You can keep going and still own it. The load is the same either way. It is only the hand on it that changes. There is one thing today you choose to carry rather than have dropped on you. Take it up on purpose, and do one hour on it that way. That is the harder end of patience — holding without forcing.
cells.sheetLine: You have been holding this. You just have not claimed it.

attempts.check: The record says Resilience is carved by a history that tested it; I can only render the persistence itself, not what happened, who was involved, how long ago, or what it cost — the Too Little core stays with the door, not the story behind it. A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not holding the reason to keep going; I'm just tired,' so the asks hold whether or not the person names the star. The ask survives a wrong read because it's one visible act with a finish — write the thing down once; say the reason out loud to one person — not a test of whether the diagnosis fits. The sentence that would serve me more than them is 'You picked your star and now you keep going': it assigns a motive the record only implies, and I've cut it.
